sentences.text: In life, Elektorornis was slightly smaller than a modern sparrow.
Alexander D. Clark and Jingmai O'Connor (2021) concluded that Elektorornis likely had a toothless beak to pry into wood, using its elongated toe to acquire prey.
This animal belongs to the parent group Enantiornithes and is classified in the class Reptilia.
Elektorornis lived during the Cenomanian stage, between 100.5 and 93.9 million years ago.
